items.title: Stand up the identity directory with every grant rooted in a person
items.summary: The standalone identity directory: sign-in through the platform's own Rauthy fork, two upstream providers linked to one person, a signed authoritative identity, and the standalone screen journey, all installed against one PostgreSQL database. It is the root every later grant in the platform hangs from.

provenance.context: The identity platform statement (docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md) and IDENTITY-001; the cluster and its five briefs reached main in 55933549.

items.notes: The briefs build in order: DIRECTORY-002 before 003, 003 before 004 and 005. Each card runs through the board (brief_card, then card_build_v3).

items.title: Build the secrets broker so agents hold handles, never credentials
items.summary: A broker that keeps credentials behind handles: the door swaps a handle for the credential at use, the token revolver is the first consumer, and rotation and sealing happen without any agent ever seeing a secret.

provenance.context: The secrets cluster (docs/design/secrets) and its two briefs, written to ADR-001 and ADR-002.

items.title: Move the Rauthy fork onto the next hardened upstream release
items.summary: Rebase the platform's own Rauthy fork (ADR-009) onto the next upstream release that upstream tags as a release and whose changelog carries security or hardening fixes. Our commits stay on top of the upstream tag, unsquashed and unaltered; the pin moves to the rebased head; the fork builds and passes its own suite; the standalone install comes up from the rebased build against the existing database with no migration by hand; the provider-link behaviour of DIRECTORY-004 still holds.

provenance.context: Written ahead of its trigger from the Lys board card of the same name. Upstream was still v0.36.2 on 2026-09-23 and the fork is pinned to that exact version. The trigger is a fact recorded in the pull request (the upstream tag, its commit, its changelog entry), never a judgement.

items.notes: The card is built only when the trigger is met. It needs DIRECTORY-004 (the provider link commit the rebase must carry) and DIRECTORY-002 (the standalone install it must prove) landed first. If the rebase cannot carry a fork commit cleanly the card stops and reports the conflicting upstream commit rather than rewriting ours. Nothing in Cambium or Aion changes; no production node is touched; Tom's three acts stay Tom's.

items.title: Rewrite the decision quotes as plain statements in the team's words

items.title: Give a session a home: its context record, kept byte for byte
items.summary: The home (identity platform steps 4 and 5): a running session's transcript captured into a home byte for byte, indexed for reading back, with the record of what the agent was given as well as what it did. Lanterns, translation and forks stand on it.

provenance.context: CONTEXT-001 (docs/design/identity/briefs) and the home cluster, landed on main with lys PR 8 (HOME-001, design.json, stories, checklist).

items.notes: Owned by Archie. The home cluster and HOME-001 landed on main with PR 8; the cached-index rule (lys-home Index::from_cached) is in that brief. Next: HOME-001 dispatched through the board.

items.title: Launch a session from its home on Claude Code through a kept template
items.summary: The home keeps a launch template per harness, starting with Claude Code, as an object named by its hash; lys-home render-launch turns a template and a session into the files a Claude Code launch needs and a printed launch line that resumes the rendered file by path, and records each render on the session so a stranger can tell which template a session was launched with.

provenance.quote: A session's home holds the pieces a new session is made from, the record, the canon and the handover, but nothing yet turns them into a running session on a given harness. Tom ruled at 16:00 on 22 September that the home keeps a preset template per harness which maps the pieces onto that harness, and that the mapping covers the MCP configuration, the environment variables, which secrets the session may read and which it may only use through a handle, what is appended to the system prompt, and where the prior conversation goes, delivered as files and runtime variables, command mappings in text, never a transcript converter. The change is a launch template for Claude Code, kept in the home as a versioned object beside the record, with its schema in docs/design/home, and a lys-home subcommand that reads a template and a session and writes the files a Claude Code launch needs. The files are the rendered JSONL under the chosen uuid and cwd as R4 renders it, an MCP configuration file, an environment file, an appended instructions file, and the launch line that resumes by path as R9 states. The template has named slots. The transcript slot is the one slot no template can map generically, so the template names how this harness fills it, and Claude Code fills it by resuming the rendered file by path. A secret named in the template is written as its handle and never as its value, and the launch line reads the value through the broker at start, which the secrets rows own. Every render of a template records the template hash, the session head hash and the written paths in a lys.harness_event entry on the session, so a stranger can tell which template a session was launched with. The subcommand prints a JSON report of hashes and paths and never prints transcript, block or body content, and a missing argument exits 2 naming it. Acceptance is that a fixture template and the recorded session from PROOF-RESUME render to a directory whose files match recorded hashes, that the printed launch line resumes the rendered path with the template's flags, that a template naming a secret writes only the handle and a search of the written files for the fixture value finds nothing, that rendering the same template and session twice yields identical hashes, and that a template with an unknown slot is refused by name. Not in scope are any harness other than Claude Code, launching on another machine, and the broker's own read. Filed by Archie on Tom's 16:00 ruling of 22 September 2026 and HOME-001 R4, R9 and R12 on lys main 0073b966, at 06:15 on 26 September 2026.
provenance.context: Filed on the ruling relayed at docs/design/identity/STATEMENT-2026-09-22.md line 181 and HOME-001 R4, R9 and R12, on lys main 0073b966; the card lead's answers on fork-on-resume, the fixture, use-only secrets, the unbuilt broker reader, the side-leaf event, the canon and the ruling's record are written into HOME-002.

items.notes: Further units, not written: Wire the secret slot's start-time read to the broker once SECRETS-002 lands; Launch from the template and capture the new session into the same home; Canon and handover slots in the launch template; Target profiles: sandbox and VM rendered from the template (P8); Launch on a second machine from a fetched home (stage 3); Templates for a second harness; manifold seat document consuming the printed launch line.

items.title: Record what a session was given at render: the lys.given context record
items.summary: At every launch-template render, lys-home appends a lys.given custom entry after the render event. It names each instruction document Claude Code will load for the session's working directory, and each file the render wrote, by path, byte length and SHA-256, in the load order measured on a named Claude Code version, with the environment variable names the template set and the kinds resolved and left unlisted, and never a document's content. Two subcommands list those records and check a file on disk against one by hash. This is step 4's context record: what a session was given, unsigned and unencrypted, shaped as hashes so that signing and encryption can be added later.

provenance.quote: Step 4 is what a session was given, not only what it did. When Claude Code starts a session it reads instruction documents the person did not type: the CLAUDE.md chain from the working directory upward, the user's own CLAUDE.md, the memory index the seat loads, the appended instructions file the launch template writes, the MCP configuration, and the names of the environment variables set for it. Today the launch template's render event records the template hash, the session head hash and the written paths, and nothing records which of those documents the session was given, in what versions and order. This card records that as the context record: at render, the template subcommand resolves the documents Claude Code will load for the rendered session's working directory and the home's own files it wrote, reads each one, and appends to the session, after the render event, a lys.given custom entry listing every document in the order the harness reads them, each as its path, its byte length and its SHA-256, with the harness name and version the order was measured on, and never a document's content. The resolution is measured, not assumed: the brief names the Claude Code version on this Mac and the order it loads instruction files in, from its own behaviour, and the proof document records that measurement. A lys-home subcommand lists a session's given records with their documents, and a second checks a listed document against a file on disk by hash, saying matches or differs and never printing either. The record is unsigned and the content is not encrypted: signing is stage 6 and comes when asked for, and encryption at rest is a stage 3 precondition card; the given entry names hashes only, so both can be added later without changing what is recorded. Acceptance is that rendering the fixture template for a fixture working directory holding a CLAUDE.md and a memory index appends a lys.given entry after the render event whose documents are those files plus the written appended instructions and MCP configuration, in the measured order, with lengths and hashes that match the files; that rendering twice gives two given entries whose document lists are identical; that changing one byte of the fixture CLAUDE.md changes exactly that document's hash in the next given entry; that the check subcommand says matches for the recorded file and differs after the change; that the given entry and the listing hold no document content, checked by a search for a fixture sentence; and that one real session render on this Mac is recorded in the proof document as hashes, counts and paths only. Not in scope: signing or anchoring the record, which is stage 6; encryption at rest; recording documents a session reads later by its own tools; harnesses other than Claude Code. This card stands on the launch template card, ct98Wv-2, and is built on main after it lands. Filed by Archie on his 22 September 2026 statement in lys that step 4 is what the agent was given, Tom's 16:00 22 September 2026 template ruling that every render is a receipted event, his 16:27 ruling that signing comes when asked for, and home DESIGN P7 and P8 at lys main 0073b966, on 26 September 2026.
provenance.context: A Cambium card on the home cluster, standing on the launch template card ct98Wv-2; the lead's answers settled the environment names member, the kinds member, what identical document lists mean, the order within one directory, that files reaching the request by @-import or from .claude/rules are recorded, given-check's exit status, and that the render's entry names @-imports and .claude/rules as unlisted kinds while a second entry at the first request records what reached the model.

items.notes: Renumbered from the HOME-002 it was written as, since the launch template took HOME-002 and RM-006 first; built on the launch template branch (RM-006, lys PR 14) and lands after it. Built on lys main after ct98Wv-2 lands. Further units, not written: Record settings.json in the given entry; Record SessionStart hook output in the given entry; Record plugin skill and agent listings in the given entry; Record output styles in the given entry; Record what reached the model, @-imports and .claude/rules included, in a second lys.given entry at the first request from the HOME-001 proxy's capture.

items.title: Light a lantern in the home and recall it by note and by point
items.summary: Stage 5 of the home: a lantern is a note plus a point in a session, lit on purpose as a lys.lantern custom entry at the session's head, whose note grows only by lys.lantern_epilogue entries. Three lys-home subcommands light one, add an epilogue, and recall lanterns by an exact case-folded phrase of their note or epilogues, or by session and entry id, printing the lantern and its epilogues and never the transcript around the point. A lantern lives in the home and is never rendered into a Claude Code resume file.

provenance.quote: A lantern is a note plus a point in a transcript, declared on purpose at a moment of completion, success or learning, never automatically; it is what a later session, or a fork, walks back to. The home holds sessions in Pi's grammar and adds nothing to that grammar, so a lantern is a lys.lantern custom entry appended at the session's head, carrying the point it marks as the id of an existing entry in that session, the note as written, who lit it and when. The point may be any entry on the session's tree, not only the head, so a lantern can mark a place the session has already moved past. A note is append-only and grows: an epilogue is a lys.lantern_epilogue custom entry naming the lantern's own entry id and carrying the further words, so a lantern's story is its entry followed by its epilogues in order, and nothing is ever rewritten. A lys-home subcommand lights one: it takes the home, the session, the entry id of the point and the note, refuses by name a point that is not an entry of that session and an empty note, appends the entry, and prints a JSON report of the lantern's id, session, point and time. A second subcommand adds an epilogue to a named lantern. A third recalls: by note, listing every lantern in the home whose note or epilogues contain the given words, exact and case-folded, no vectors; and by point, listing every lantern that marks a given session and entry id. Each listing row is the lantern's id, session, point, lit-by, lit-at, note, and its epilogues, and never a line of the transcript around the point. A lantern is not rendered into a Claude Code resume file; it lives in the home. Acceptance is that on a fixture session a lantern lit at a past entry is recalled by a word of its note and by its point; that two lanterns on the same point are both recalled by point; that an epilogue is recalled with its lantern, after it, and recall by a word that appears only in the epilogue finds the lantern; that lighting at an unknown entry id and lighting with an empty note are each refused by name; that after lighting, the session file's earlier bytes are unchanged and the head is the lantern entry; that the rendered Claude Code file of that session contains no lantern line; and that no listing prints transcript content, checked by a search for a fixture message's text. Not in scope: the fork through a lantern, which is stage 5b and its own card; resonance, whispers, vectors and any ranking; dimming by code churn; Norn's tables; Cambium's screen. Filed by Archie on Tom's definition of 8 August 2026 that a lantern is a note plus a pathway back, declared deliberately, notes append-only, his roadmap stage 5 of 22 September 2026, and home DESIGN P2 and P7 at lys main 0073b966, on 26 September 2026.
provenance.context: The stage 5 lantern card on the Lys board, surveyed against lys main 0073b966; the lead of the home card answered the survey's open questions (phrase matching, the P7 and CN3 exception, held sessions, blank notes and epilogues, epilogue authorship, unknown points in recall, lanterns as points) and HOME-004 carries those answers.

items.notes: HOME-004 is the first unit. Further units, not yet written: Stage 5b: fork through a lantern (cut at its point and seed a new session); Lit-by from a directory identity rather than a declared name; Lighting from a live session under capture (the door's proxy or harness hook); Cambium's lantern screen; Recall by resonance and vectors, with ranking and churn dimming.

items.title: Make the Claude Code render byte-deterministic for the same session head and version
items.summary: Two renders of the same session head give different bytes whenever the context path holds an entry whose id is not uuid-shaped, which the importer writes for every tool record with more than one result: the render draws a fresh random uuid for each. The render derives those uuids from the record instead (UUIDv5 over a fixed lys namespace, the session id and the entry id with its role), a fixture carrying the defect is pinned by hash in a test and in PROOF-RESUME.md, and the resume is re-measured on the Claude Code installed on this Mac. A rendered file can then be told by its hash, a receipted render event can name what was written, and the launch template's identical-hash acceptance has ground to stand on.

provenance.quote: The Claude Code render in crates/lys-home walks a session's context path and writes the JSONL file that Claude Code 2.1.282 on this Mac resumes by path, as HOME-001 R4 and R9 landed it on lys main 0073b966. Rendering the same session twice does not give the same bytes today when a tool record on the path holds more than one result, which the translation card's survey found on 26 September 2026 while reading the render for the Codex rollout, and the launch template card's acceptance that rendering the same template and session twice yields identical hashes stands on the render being deterministic. A render of the same session head with the same lys-home version is one function of the record and must give the same bytes every time, so a reader can tell a rendered file by its hash and a receipted render event can name what was written. The change finds why two renders of a multi-result tool record differ, names that cause in the proof document, and makes the render byte-deterministic for the same session head and the same version without changing what the rendered file holds or how Claude Code resumes it. Where the cause is an order that the record does not fix, the render takes the order the record gives, entry order then part order, and never a map's or a set's order; where the cause is a fresh id or a clock, the value is derived from the record's own ids and stamps as the fork and launch cards derive theirs. Acceptance is that a fixture session holding a tool record with more than one result renders twice to files of equal SHA-256; that the fixture from PROOF-RESUME renders twice to equal hashes; that a recorded fixture hash in the proof document matches the render at the landed commit; that the rendered file still resumes in Claude Code 2.1.282 on this Mac, recorded in the proof document as before; and that the proof document names the cause found. Not in scope: any change to the importer, the record's shape, or the rendered file's content beyond the determinism, and any harness other than Claude Code. Filed by Archie on the translation card's survey of 26 September 2026, on Tom's rule of 16 September 2026 to find the underlying cause, and on lys main 0073b966.
provenance.context: Filed on the translation card's survey, which found the nondeterminism while reading the render for the Codex rollout; surveyed on lys main 0073b966. The lead's answers settled the Claude Code version the resume is measured on (the one installed when the proof runs, as `claude --version` prints it, with the rendered records' version field left at 2.1.281) and that this card defines the id derivation the fork and launch cards follow; a follow-up card ruled that the derived uuid is salted with the session id.

items.notes: Renumbered from the HOME-002 and RM-006 it was written as, since the launch template took HOME-002 and RM-006, the context record HOME-003 and RM-007, and the lanterns HOME-004 and RM-008 first. Stands on HOME-001's render (R4) and CLI (R9), already on main at 0073b966, so no roadmap dependency is written. Further units, not written: Make the Claude Code import deterministic for the same transcript; Render tool parts from the stored block so a round trip adds only the new turn; Move the render's default Claude Code version off 2.1.281. ADR-016 is proposed and binds the fork and launch cards' id derivation.

items.title: Fork a session from a lantern's point and launch the child
items.summary: Stage 5b of the home: lys-home fork takes a lantern id, resolves it to the session it was lit in, cuts that session's chain at the last assistant message at or before the lantern's point, and writes a child session holding the parent's own lines with its ancestry on both sides (the header's parentSession, a lys.forked_from entry in the child, a lys.fork entry at the parent's head), adding nothing to the block store and rewriting nothing in the parent. A user-message point is carried as a seed prompt the child's render writes beside the rendered file and the launch line passes as the first prompt. The child renders and launches through the launch template, measured on the installed Claude Code version.

provenance.quote: A lantern is a pathway back to a conversation with the self that lit it, and Claude Code resumes a session only from its end. This brief delivers the fork that makes the pathway: a new session in the home cut from the parent's chain at a lantern's point, carrying its ancestry on both sides, adding nothing to the block store and rewriting nothing in the parent, then rendered and launched like any session. It is stage 5b of the home and stands on the lantern card's lys.lantern entry (the design's solution and ADR-012).
provenance.context: The stage 5b fork card on the Lys board, surveyed against lys main after the lantern card; the lead's answers settled that the fork stands on the lantern card and is built on the main it lands on, that the child launches through the launch template's line, that the copied lines are the parent's own bytes with the same hashes and the block store unchanged, that lys.forked_from is the first entry the fork writes, that parentSession carries the parent file's path as Pi reads it, that a user-message point is carried as a seed and never dropped, that a lantern resolves to its lit-in session (lit_in) with the older-record rule until the lantern card records it, that a lantern before any assistant message is refused nothing_to_fork, and that non-text parts of a carried message are counted, never refused. HOME-006 carries those answers.

items.notes: Renumbered from the HOME-002 it was written as; HOME-006 follows the lantern card (HOME-004, RM-008) and the launch template (HOME-002, RM-006), both on main, and after the render card (HOME-007), which took RM-009, ADR-016, C31 to C35, S18, S19 and CN9. Further units, not written: lit_in written by the light act (the lantern card's next round); a fork given tools, a lens or a briefing on what changed since the point; leases, budgets and kill rules; harnesses other than Claude Code.

items.title: Judge the hand-built HOME-001 code at 0073b966 through the chain and set its cards by row
items.summary: The chain's whole judgement over crates/lys-home at 0073b966, recorded in one proof document (docs/design/home/PROOF-CHAIN.md) without changing the crate: Jev per file, the gate's seven deterministic legs, ast-grep recorded as not measured, each finding its own line checked against current main, and each of the seven step 5 cards given done or in review by row, set on the board after a green landing.

provenance.quote:
The HOME-001 rows R1 to R11 were built by hand on 24 September 2026 and reached lys main through the merge 7b47115, before Tom's rule of 25 September that every carded row goes through its board's chain. The seven cards that carry those rows on the step 5 board sit in review with no chain fields, and nothing on main says the chain has judged that code. This card adds no new code and only proves what is already there. It runs the chain's whole judgement over crates/lys-home as it stands on main at 0073b966: Jev per file, fmt, clippy pedantic, tests, ast-grep and the gate. The brief names each check and the command it runs, and the build's proof document records each check's outcome on the crate as found, with the commit it was measured on. If every check passes the build lands with only the proof document and the design rows this card needs. If Jev or the gate finds something, the build records each finding as its own line in the proof document and lands without changing the crate; each finding then becomes a card of its own on the step 5 board, worded from that line. When this card lands green the seven cards are set to done and each points at this card's landing, so that done means judged by the chain and never just merged before the rule. Acceptance is that the proof document names the commit, every check by name and its outcome, and holds no code changes to crates/lys-home; that a reader can rerun each named command at that commit and see the same outcome; and that the landing is green through src_pr and src_land with Jev and the gate. Not in scope: any new capability in lys-home, any change to the eleven rows, or any card other than the seven named. This card builds behind the six Lys briefs in the one-build queue on this Mac under the load guard. Filed by Archie on Waffles' ruling of 07:08 on 26 September 2026 in the Cambium channel, on Tom's rule of 22:26 on 25 September 2026 that every carded row goes through the chain, and on lys main 0073b966.

Rulings of the lead, Archie, given on 27 September 2026 to the run a6d7b86a-aba7-4110-a5a7-7331405de7d3 in answer to its rounds. That run took every answer and then failed before writing, when the Argus gate refused every tool call of its session. They are settled here, and the author reopens none of them.
